issues.description: The solution implementation of Course uses the property and initializer label 'lecturer' while the problem statement and the template use 'instructor'. Additionally, other solution files (Client.swift, Developer.swift) still reference 'instructor' and call the initializer with an 'instructor' label. This mismatch is structural and will cause compilation errors and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course API consistent across all artifacts. Either rename Course.lecturer and its initializer parameter to 'instructor' in the solution (recommended to match the problem and template), or update all references and the template/problem to use 'lecturer'. Ensure the initializer label and the property name match usages in Client.swift and Developer.swift.

issues.description: The Course property for the course instructor is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement and the template use the identifier "instructor", but the solution's Course class declares the property as "lecturer". Furthermore, within the solution the Developer.attend(...) implementation still references course.instructor, creating an internal mismatch in the solution itself. This breaks the conceptual mapping for students (they expect and are instructed to use "instructor") and introduces a naming conflict that can cause confusion or compilation issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Prefer aligning the solution with the problem/template by renaming the Course property and initializer parameter from "lecturer" to "instructor" in Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift, and update any references (e.g. in Developer.swift) to use course.instructor. Alternatively, if changing the problem/template is intended, update them to use "lecturer" consistently, but ensure all code and documentation use the same name.
